# How does a single whole-body strategy reduce training conflicts in multi-object mobile tasks?

> **Current answer:** In the three-degree-of-freedom waist Unitree G1 simulation setup of ULC, skills are opened in the order of speed, height, torso/arms, combined with forward feed of arm actions with residuals, command interpolation/delay, payload randomization, and CoM reward, allowing training of a single policy that covers a large command space; evidence does not support extrapolation to complex leg actions or uncontrolled contact tasks.

- Unitree G1 with 3-DoF waist

- Isaac Lab

## Controllers and methods

- ULC unified PPO policy

## Applicable environments

- four simulation command/load/delay evaluations
- reported teleoperation tasks

## Assumptions

- Target tasks can be commanded by root velocity/height, torso orientation and arm joint positions.
- A 3-DoF-waist Unitree G1-like embodiment and procedural command sampler are available.

## Diagnosis and verification

- First verify the applicable robot, simulator, controller, environment, and assumptions, then follow the evidence locators below to inspect the original experiment or implementation.

## Result

- In the three-degree-of-freedom waist Unitree G1 simulation setup of ULC, skills are opened in the order of speed, height, torso/arms, combined with forward feed of arm actions with residuals, command interpolation/delay, payload randomization, and CoM reward, allowing training of a single policy that covers a large command space; evidence does not support extrapolation to complex leg actions or uncontrolled contact tasks.

## Limitations

- Target tasks can be commanded by root velocity/height, torso orientation and arm joint positions.
- A 3-DoF-waist Unitree G1-like embodiment and procedural command sampler are available.
